name: Al-Ula International Airport
before:
The airport for Al-Ula in north west Saudi Arabia, and the closest one to Hegra, the pre-Islamic archaeological site, and to the Al-Ula Heritage Village.

It is worth knowing what this airport is for. It was the first in Saudi Arabia designed specifically to serve people coming to the region to visit, rather than domestic or business traffic.

It has grown very fast. It opened in October 2011 as a domestic airport with a first flight from Riyadh, built for 100,000 passengers a year. International flights were approved in March 2021 and an expansion lifted capacity to 400,000, at which point it was renamed Al-Ula International. A further expansion announced in October 2023 is meant to take it to 6 million passengers a year and add a logistics role for the north west of the kingdom.

It was originally named after Prince Abdul Majeed bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, so older references use that name.
after:
The airport for AlUla in north west Saudi Arabia. Built for 100,000 passengers a year, it was expanded to 400,000 and approved for international flights in March 2021. In October 2023 the Royal Commission for AlUla unveiled designs for a second terminal that would take capacity to 6 million a year and make the airport a logistics hub for the north west.

It was originally named after Prince Abdul Majeed bin Abdulaziz, so older references use that name.
